User approved Augustus through the fall of the Western Empire in 476, including Eastern contemporaries, rivals, breakaway imperial rulers and documented claimants. Julius Caesar is an explicit house-rule exception: he was dictator, not emperor. One person per catch, not one reign. The core chronology https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Roman_emperors was reconciled with https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Roman_usurpers , the specialist DIR index, and all eight linked Livius chronology sections beginning https://www.livius.org/articles/misc/list-of-roman-emperors/ . Later Byzantine rulers are outside the date scope. Alleged claims and uncertain identities are admitted under the broad claimant convention and identified as uncertain in blurbs; these are not 183 universally recognized emperors. Definite fictional inventions and nonclaiming rebels are excluded. Qualified Pseudo-Neros are separate claimants. Sabinus Julianus and the separately reported claimant under Maximian are separate, with the identification dispute disclosed. Caesar maps to Julius Caesar; Constantine to I, Claudius to I, Theodosius to I, Valentinian to I, Severus to Septimius, Constantius to II (the less rare represented owner), Marcus to Marcus Aurelius, Julian to the Apostate and Gordian to III. Other numbered or claimant forms require qualifiers. Source chronology dates differ on some ancient events; blurbs do not imply consensus on disputed claims. Partial-name fairness: Julius belongs to Julius Caesar (10), Maximus to Magnus Maximus (85), and Macrianus to Macrianus Minor; distinguishing rival names still have separate exact catches.

questions.prompt: Game Modes in Madden or FIFA
questions.sourceNote: Curated general-trivia recall rarity, not measured response frequencies: 10/30/60/85/100; 15 is the separate QUIRKY exception. See coverage-audit.json for source reconciliation and edge decisions. User approved named modes and submodes from any Madden, FIFA or EA Sports FC edition, including historical console, World Cup, Street and mobile releases. Edition renames of the same mode share a catch; independently named gameplay submodes and drills can score separately. EA manuals and feature inventories form the baseline, supplemented by historical manuals and a series-mode index; game-evidence.json maps every included group to sources. Creative checks covered story campaigns, party games, training, career roles, competitive ladders, street rules and mobile formats. There is no complete historical cross-platform catalogue, and rotating events may leave undiscovered names; this is a researched open bank, not a claim of a proven finite inventory. Generic Ultimate Team means FIFA/FC; MUT means Madden. Career/Manager means Manager Career; generic Seasons, Friendlies and Draft refer to their FIFA forms. Gauntlet means the Madden Skills Trainer challenge; FUT/MUT Gauntlet require qualifiers. Rush belongs to FUT Rush, Arena to FIFA Practice Arena, Moments to FUT Moments, The League to Superstar, and House Rules to FIFA; distinct Madden/mobile versions require their qualifiers. Squad and game format variants sharing the same mode name are not multiplied by annual edition. Store, roster editor, rewards track, difficulty and cosmetic menu names are not standalone game modes. Existing matcher limitation: generic fragments such as Madden or Mode may suggest an unrelated specific mode and require confirmation; these are not intentional aliases.

User explicitly expanded this prompt to include established slang, home-run types and plain descriptions such as two-run home run. Distinct general slang expressions are separate catches; spelling/tense variants share a catch. Equivalent subtype wording is grouped: grand salami with Grand slam; oppo taco/oppo boppo with Opposite-field home run. Canonical Home run/HR belongs to Homer. Central sources: MLB's nickname inventory https://www.mlb.com/cut4/ranking-the-26-best-nicknames-for-a-home-run-c294721188 , the MLB glossary, Dickson dictionary https://www.baseball-almanac.com/dictionary-term.php?term=home+run and https://www.baseball-almanac.com/dictionary-term.php?term=circuit , plus https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_baseball_terms . Additional sources and included terms are mapped in home-evidence.json. Coverage spans general slang, run totals, ball flight/direction, game situation, substitutions, consecutive hits and established ballpark terms. No finite global inventory exists, especially for regional slang and arbitrary compound descriptions. Only documented forms are included rather than generating every adjective combination. Little League home run is QUIRKY 15: the established phrase describes an error-assisted trip, not an official statistical home run; independently documented by https://sabr.org/little-league-home-runs . An obsolete offensive historical term is identified as such, without endorsing its usage. Grand slam, walk-off grand slam and ultimate grand slam require their own qualifiers; the last specifically erases a three-run deficit.

User explicitly included Darnell Hillman, winner of the NBA's season-long 1976–77 competition, at 100; primary confirmation https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/darnell-hillman-fred-jones-announced-as-slam-dunk-judges . The 1976 Julius Erving contest was ABA and does not qualify. Years without a contest create no answer. John Wall is the 2014 individual winner in the NBA list; team participation alone does not add Paul George. Keshad Johnson is the 2026 winner. Useful surnames and initials count; bare Robinson belongs to Nate, bare Jones to Derrick. Glenn Robinson III and Fred Jones require their distinguishing names. Larry Nance means the 1984-winning father, not his nonwinning son.

Exactly the 168 primes p with 2 <= p < 1000, one numeric answer per catch. Generated with the sieve of Eratosthenes, independently verified by trial division, then compared entry-for-entry with the complete external list at the principal source. Independent count/table corroboration: https://proofwiki.org/wiki/Prime_Number/Table . Neither 1 nor 1000 qualifies. Blurbs state calculated ordinal position; 2 and 997 have boundary facts. Scores rise broadly with recall difficulty and magnitude, with familiar anchors such as 101, 127, 257, 521 and 997 adjusted downward. Numeric spellings only keep composite numbers from becoming autocorrect suggestions; prime names in words are not separate catches. Existing runtime limitation: punctuation normalization strips a minus sign, so -2 normalizes to the valid answer 2. Negative numbers are not editorially eligible; fixing numeric sign handling would require a separate game-code change.
